Primeval

/pry-MEE-vul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Primeval means belonging to the earliest, most ancient period of the world; primitive and original.

Primeval means belonging to the earliest, most ancient period of the world; primitive and original. Mist drifted between the giant ferns, giving the swamp a primeval look, as if dinosaurs might still wade through it.

Worked Example

On the gorge floor, the survey team measured cedars that had been alive for more than two thousand years. No road had ever reached the grove, no axe had ever touched it, and the tangled understory grew exactly as it had before the surrounding valleys were farmed. Standing under the canopy, the team's botanist whispered that they were looking at a primeval forest, a living remnant of the world's earliest age.

The untouched grove has survived unchanged from the earliest era of the world, which is exactly what primeval describes.

How Primeval Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

primal

primal: first in time; original and instinctive

ancient

ancient: dating from the distant past

Antonyms

modern

modern: belonging to the present era

newfangled

newfangled: recently invented, often needlessly novel

How Strong Is It? — age-old → primordial → primeval

age-old vs. primeval

age-old vs. primeval: An age-old custom stretches back many generations, while something primeval belongs to the earliest era of the world itself.

primordial vs. primeval

primordial vs. primeval: Primeval describes the world's first ages, but primordial reaches back even further, to the very beginning of existence, before life had fully taken shape.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of primeval.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — prim

Root — prim: from Latin primus, first

Root — ev

Root — ev: from Latin aevum, an age or era

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: characteristic of, having the nature of

Put it together

Put it together: Primeval fuses Latin primus, 'first,' with aevum, 'an age or era,' and seals them with the suffix -al, 'characteristic of.' Latin primaevus meant 'of the first age,' so a primeval forest is literally characteristic of the world's very first age.

Use the root in a new word: longevity

Use the root in a new word: longevity: The giant tortoise's longevity, literally its 'long age,' comes from the same Latin root aevum that gives primeval its sense of deep time.

Root Check

Word Choice

literary, scientific register

Primeval belongs to deep time: primeval forests, primeval oceans, primeval instincts inherited from our earliest ancestors. Use it for things dating to the world's first ages, not merely for anything old; a century-old house is historic, not primeval.
